skills.content:
---
name: print-design
description: >-
  Use when designing or revising a custom 3D-printable part, case, or enclosure
  from the user's measurements or test-print feedback.
---
# Parametric print design
1. Get real measurements (photos with a ruler help). Add clearance beyond hand measurements (about 0.5-1.5 mm depending on fit) since they may be slightly off.
2. Model parametrically in OpenSCAD so sizes are easy to tweak; prefer no purchased hardware unless the user has it on hand (ask for exact screw sizes, including head height).
3. Verify before sending: watertight mesh, no overlapping parts, moving parts (hinges, slides) clear their sweep, no floating islands, overhangs printable without supports.
4. Mirror guard: confirm each print-oriented STL, moved back to its assembled pose, matches the assembled part, so cutouts don't end up on the wrong side.
5. Render previews (front, section, exploded, assembly) and send them with the STLs plus print settings for the user's printer and slicer (orientation, brim, layer height, material).
6. Pick material for the job: PLA for fit tests, PETG for anything near heat. Keep simple shapes simple to avoid stringing and needless travel.
7. For big parts, offer a quick fit-test slice first.
8. After each test print, ask for a photo, diagnose (check the part's orientation before changing dimensions), and version the design (v2, v3) while keeping older versions.

skills.content:
---
name: print-forge-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner of the print forge template: learn their
  3D printer and slicer setup.
---
I help you find, tweak, and design 3D-printable models, and dial in slicing and print settings.
Ask one at a time:
1. Which printer do you have (and any multi-material unit)?
2. Which slicer do you use?
3. Which filaments do you usually have on hand?
4. Any hardware on hand for builds (screw sizes, magnets), or should designs avoid bought parts?
5. What would you like to make first?
Save answers 1-4 as profile memories, then start on their first project using the print-design skill.
